meta.title: RFQ: lower line 1 and raise line 2 (90 and 55)
gaps: Set the initial RFQ prices to 100 on line 1 and 50 on line 2 using the vendor portal.
Revise line 1 to 90 while revising line 2 to 55 in the same submission.
Verify the conditional per-line refusal for the raised line with the exact message "You cannot increase the price" when increases are blocked.
warnings: can only test part of this — no step for: Set the initial RFQ prices to 100 on line 1 and 50 on line 2 using the vendor portal.; Revise line 1 to 90 while revising line 2 to 55 in the same submission.; Verify the conditional per-line refusal for the raised line with the exact message "You cannot increase the price" when increases are blocked.

steps.note: Create an RFQ event for the vendor revision scenario.
Configure the event as an RFQ rather than the default auction.
Apply the RFQ pricing template before adding line items.
Create the two RFQ lines required by the scenario.
Complete the RFQ pricing sheet so the event can be published.
Invite the QA vendor who will submit and revise the bid.
Publish the RFQ before entering the vendor portal.
Confirm the RFQ reached a real published project page.
Move to the invited vendor's separate supplier-portal session.
Open the live RFQ pricing sheet in the vendor portal.
Submit an initial vendor bid; the catalog applies this value to every price cell.
Confirm the initial vendor quote was accepted.
Submit a same-vendor revision, exercising the available revision flow even though it cannot target only line 1.
Confirm the revision submission was accepted.
